first_impression.reaction: Our daughter sent this because New Zealand is now the front runner. I was relieved before I'd finished the first paragraph: yes, it's legal, and no, they don't need to be citizens. I read it all on the iPad. It's calm and orderly, and it reads like someone who has actually done the paperwork. The Medicare line about Mum is worth the whole page to me, and so are the deposits and level access questions. The earthquake and volcano paragraph gave me a fright, though, and I still don't know who we ring on the day if something goes wrong, or who gets Mum from the airport to a lodge in the mountains.

journey.quote: Yes, you can get married in New Zealand as Australians, and you do not need to be New Zealand citizens: visitors to New Zealand can marry there.
journey.reaction: Good. That's Geoff's first question answered in the first line. I can forward this paragraph as it is.

journey.quote: It won't, quite. There is a form to sign before you leave Australia, a registry office to visit after you land, and a certificate to prepare for home.
journey.reaction: I like that it doesn't pretend it's all easy just because it's close. Three steps, in order. I can follow that.

journey.section: Practical notes for you and your guests
journey.quote: Medical facilities are of a similar standard to Australia's, and a reciprocal health care agreement lets Australians access public medical care by showing an Australian passport and a valid Medicare card.
journey.reaction: This is the line I'll read out to Mum. Her Medicare card works over there. That takes a real weight off.

journey.section: Practical notes for you and your guests
journey.quote: Travel insurance still matters for everyone travelling.
journey.reaction: Sensible, and it says everyone, not just the couple. I'll make sure the older ones have it.

journey.section: Practical notes for you and your guests
journey.quote: An Australian driver's licence is not approved ID for buying alcohol or entering licensed premises, so guests heading to a bar after the reception should carry their passport.
journey.reaction: I'd never have thought of that. A small thing, but it tells me whoever wrote this has thought about the guests, not only the bride.

journey.quote: Those two numbers set your window. Apply too late and there is no licence on the day; apply too early and it lapses before the wedding.
journey.reaction: Clear. That's the sort of mistake that costs money, and now I know to ask the children when they are lodging it.

journey.quote: For an outdoor wedding, the back-up is your wet-weather plan in legal form, so name it with care.
journey.reaction: Very practical. I'd have assumed you could just move inside if it rained. Glad someone said it.

journey.quote: Celebrants set their own fees on top of the licence fee.
journey.reaction: Fair enough, but there isn't a single figure anywhere for the licence, the certificate or the Apostille. I'd like a rough idea, in dollars, so I know what we're agreeing to.

journey.section: When to get married in New Zealand
journey.quote: Earthquakes are a constant risk, large damaging quakes can happen at any time, and all of New Zealand's coastline is at risk of a tsunami.
journey.reaction: Goodness. I'm glad it's honest and quotes the government, but then volcanoes and being stranded follow straight after, and nothing says who looks after the family if it happens.

journey.quote: Ask your venue how guests travel in from Auckland for your dates.
journey.reaction: That's exactly my question, and the page hands it back to us. Who arranges the transfers for older guests?

journey.quote: **Security:** how does your security work, and how would it work alongside a private team we bring?
journey.reaction: A private team? We're a family from Glen Waverley. This one isn't for us. I skipped it.

journey.quote: **Deposits and contracts:** whose name is on the contract, in which currency are payments made, and when do deposits become non-refundable?
journey.reaction: There it is. Whose name, which currency, when the money is gone. That's what I'd ask, and it's in writing.

journey.quote: **Access:** which ceremony, dining and guest spaces have level access?
journey.reaction: Mum and her walking frame. Someone thought about us.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you as one point of contact from start to finish, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: One person, AUD, fee in writing first. That's what I want when it's our money. I'd still like a name and a phone number.

unanswered_questions: Who do we ring if something goes wrong on the wedding weekend, after hours? Is anyone from Wedded Wonderland there on the day? (deferred business detail)
Do you arrange airport transfers for guests, including an elderly guest with a walking frame, to a lodge in Queenstown or the Bay of Islands? (deferred business detail)
Are our deposits protected if a New Zealand lodge or supplier, or Wedded Wonderland itself, fails?
Roughly what do the licence, certificate and Apostille cost, and does Wedded Wonderland handle that paperwork or is it all on the couple? (fee amounts deferred)
How is your fee charged, roughly what range, and do you take commissions from venues? (deferred business detail)
If an earthquake, volcano alert or road closure hits the week of the wedding, what happens to our money and the plan?
Is the first conversation a phone call with a real person, and can I join it as a parent paying part?
Have you planned real weddings in New Zealand I could look at? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: New Zealand has several active volcanoes, and alert levels can rise quickly, with evacuation ordered at short notice.
turn_offs_found.why: Not a tone problem, it's honest and calm. But coming straight after earthquakes and tsunamis, and before being stranded, it leaves me worried about Mum, and nothing afterwards tells me who would look after the family or what happens to deposits. My fear is raised and not answered.

turn_offs_found.quote: Lodges, vineyard estates and private homes are the usual settings for a New Zealand wedding at this level, and each prices differently.
turn_offs_found.why: 'At this level', then drones and a private security team underneath. It isn't slang, but it made me feel the section was written for someone much richer than us. The deposits and access questions below it are spot on, though.

would_share_with: My husband, the intro and the recognition section, so he knows the marriage counts at home, plus the deposits and contracts question
My mother, the Medicare and reciprocal health care line, so she stops worrying about getting sick over there
My daughter, the licence window paragraph, the back-up venue line and the level access question, so she picks somewhere with Nana in mind

cta_reaction.quote: Your Wedded Advisor stays with you from start to finish, works in your time zone, quotes in AUD, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
cta_reaction.why: AUD, in writing, start to finish: all the right words. New Zealand feels manageable after reading this. But I'd talk to Geoff first, and I'd only go ahead if it's a phone call with a real person who can tell me who meets the family off the plane, who is there on the day, and how our deposits are protected.

top_3_changes: After the earthquake, volcano and weather paragraph, add one calm sentence pointing to help (for example, what Wedded Concierge does if travel is disrupted), but only if the business confirms it; otherwise flag it. The run of hazards currently ends with no reassurance.
Answer 'who gets the guests there': where the page says to ask the venue about travel from Auckland, say whether a Wedded Advisor arranges guest transfers, if the business confirms it.
Soften 'at this level' and move the security and privacy items below deposits and access, so the venue list opens with the questions a paying family asks first.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent): read top to bottom on iPad, focused on deposits, who is responsible, elderly guests, insurance and a phone call
No invented brand facts; on-the-day support, transfers, deposit protection, fees, commissions and real weddings placed in unanswered_questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored

open_questions.question: Can the business confirm on-the-day support and guest transfers so one reassuring line can follow the hazards paragraph? If not, flag rather than fill.

assumptions: Margaret arrived via a link from her daughter, reading on an iPad, as a parent contributing about half. Relevance is 3 because the page is a legal how-to written to the couple, though it covers Medicare, insurance and level access.
Likelihood to enquire is 3: deposits, AUD and fee-in-writing earn trust, but no named on-the-day help or transfers holds her back. Those are deferred business details, not penalised as must-fix.
Her mother's walking frame comes from the persona card; suburb (Glen Waverley) and husband's name (Geoff) are character colour consistent with earlier panels, not page facts.
Fast mode: full article read top to bottom, FAQ skimmed as it repeats the body.
